contests.name: Unstoppable
contests.gt_note: Hand-written from the public Damn Vulnerable DeFi challenge descriptions, not from an audit report. Solutions are public and likely in model training data: plumbing checks only, never a quality metric.

official_findings.title: Flash loan pool can be blocked by direct token transfer
official_findings.description: The contract checks that poolBalance == token.balanceOf(address(this)). A direct ERC20 transfer (bypassing depositTokens) makes poolBalance < balance, permanently bricking flash loans.

official_findings.title: Anyone can trigger flash loan on behalf of receiver, draining its ETH via fees
official_findings.description: flashLoan() does not require msg.sender == borrower. Any attacker can call flashLoan(victimContract, 0) 10 times, each time draining 1 ETH fee from the victim's balance.

official_findings.title: Flash loan executes arbitrary calldata allowing token approval theft
official_findings.description: The flashLoan function executes target.functionCall(data) with attacker-controlled target and data. Attacker encodes token.approve(attacker, MAX_UINT) as calldata, then transfers all tokens in a follow-up transaction.

official_findings.title: Reentrancy via flash loan allows stealing pool ETH
official_findings.description: During flashLoan() the attacker calls deposit() inside the IFlashLoanEtherReceiver.execute() callback with the borrowed ETH. This credits the attacker's balance in the pool accounting, satisfying the loan check. Attacker then withdraws the credited amount.

official_findings.title: Flash loan used to claim disproportionate rewards via single-block snapshot
official_findings.description: Rewards are distributed proportionally to the snapshot balance taken at the start of each 5-day round. An attacker borrows DVT tokens via flash loan, deposits them into TheRewarderPool within the same block as the snapshot, claims the majority of rewards, and repays the loan — all in one transaction.
